title: Downer Cow Syndrome & Retained Placenta
text:
Treatment and management:
- Usually, it will recover after 3 days.
- Vitamin supplementation
- Anti-inflammatory drugs
- Fly and mosquito management

2. DOWNER COW SYNDROME - the inability of the cow to rise due to muscle and nerve damage caused by prolonged recumbency.

3. RETAINED PLACENTA (Retained fetal membrane) - retention of the placenta after 24-48 hours after calving.

How to treat?
- Mechanical approach - manual removal.
- Hormonal treatment - injection of hormone such as oxytocin.

facts: Treatment and management at the top of the page notes recovery usually occurs after 3 days.
Management methods include vitamin supplementation, anti-inflammatory drugs, and fly and mosquito management.
Downer Cow Syndrome is defined as the inability of the cow to rise due to muscle and nerve damage caused by prolonged recumbency.
Slippery flooring can cause a cow to split and become a downer cow.
Malnutrition and injuries in the limbs can cause cows to go down.
Downer cow management utilizes hip locks (clamps) to hold or lift cows.
Downer cow management utilizes a harness or sling to keep the cow in a standing position.
Retained Placenta (retained fetal membrane) is defined as the retention of the placenta 24 to 48 hours after calving.
Treatment for retained placenta includes a mechanical approach involving manual removal.
Treatment for retained placenta includes hormonal treatment via injection of a hormone such as oxytocin.
